text.p: An agreement between Federal Yugoslavia and the Bosnian Serb Republic was "premature" until diplomatic relations were in place between Belgrade and Sarajevo, the State Department said on Monday.

"It is premature for the government in Belgrade, Serbia, to enter into a formal agreement with one of the entities of Bosnia and Herzegovina before full diplomatic relations have been opened between Belgrade and Sarajevo," State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns told reporters.

Burns was referring to a cooperation agreement with the Bosnian Serb Republic endorsed on Monday by the Serbian parliament, which said the pact would reinforce regional stability, according to Tanjug news agency.
It urged the federal parliament to ratify the accord which has to be accepted also by the Bosnian parliament representing all three communities in the former Yugoslav republic.

In what he called a "little shot across (Serbian President Slobodan) Milosevic's bow," Burns said Washington expected Belgrade to implement an agreement made months ago to establish full diplomatic relations with Bosnia.
"In order for an agreement between Belgrade and Pale to take effect, it must be ratified by the parliamentary assembly of Bosnia-Herzegovina," Burns said.
